content.value_statement: Complex systems slow down when reads and writes share one model. This skill guides CQRS design with commands, queries, projections, and consistency checks.
actual_capabilities: Separates command and query responsibilities with clear model boundaries.
Provides command bus and query bus implementation patterns.
Shows read model projection and synchronization workflows.
Includes FastAPI endpoint examples for command and query APIs.
Explains eventual consistency and read-your-writes handling.
limitations: Does not replace domain-specific architecture review.
Requires teams to operate separate read and write models.
May be unnecessary for simple CRUD applications.
Provided examples need adaptation and testing before production use.

use_cases.title: Split Service Workloads
use_cases.description: Separate high-traffic write workflows from read-optimized queries in a backend service.

use_cases.title: Define Architecture Boundaries
use_cases.description: Evaluate where eventual consistency is acceptable and define command, query, and projection boundaries.

use_cases.title: Plan Read Model Operations
use_cases.description: Design projection rebuilds, checkpoints, retry behavior, and recovery workflows for read models.

prompt_templates.title: Identify CQRS Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this application workflow and decide whether CQRS is appropriate. Explain the command model, query model, and cases where CRUD is better.

prompt_templates.title: Design Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CQRS design for this domain. List commands, queries, read models, consistency expectations, and validation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Projections
prompt_templates.prompt: Design projection synchronization for these events. Include checkpoints, rebuild steps, retry behavior, and stale data handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this CQRS implementation plan for failure modes. Cover idempotency, event versioning, observability, operational recovery, and performance risks.

output_examples.input: A team wants faster order search without slowing checkout writes.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends keeping checkout commands on the write model and creating an order search read model optimized for query speed.

output_examples.input: A product manager asks why reports can lag after checkout.
output_examples.output: The skill explains eventual consistency and suggests clear stale data warnings, read-your-writes flows, and acceptable lag targets.

output_examples.input: An architect needs a projection rebuild plan.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines checkpoints, event replay, retry handling, and validation steps for rebuilding read models.

best_practices: Start with workload analysis before introducing separate models.
Define acceptable consistency lag for each read use case.
Test projection rebuilds and recovery paths before launch.
anti_patterns: Using CQRS for simple CRUD screens with no scaling pressure.
Sharing database schemas so read and write models cannot evolve separately.
Ignoring stale data behavior after write operations.

faq.question: What is CQRS?
faq.answer: CQRS separates commands that change state from queries that read state.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when read and write workloads need different models, scaling, or consistency behavior.

faq.question: Does CQRS require event sourcing?
faq.answer: No. Event sourcing works well with CQRS, but CQRS can also use other persistence designs.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides implementation patterns and examples. Production systems still need adaptation, testing, and operational review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How does it handle consistency?
faq.answer: It guides eventual consistency design and read-your-writes behavior where users need immediate feedback.
